system.description:
The Toreador cloaks her words so that her intended target hears one message while everyone else present hears something else entirely, as clearly as if she'd spoken it aloud. A popular use is to "discipline" a servant or knight while outwardly praising him for a job well done, or to compliment a king's goodness in public while informing an ally that the same king is a laughable fool. In the Courts of Love, Double-Tongue lets a lady tell her knight she accepts his attentions while publicly refusing him, and it makes for an excellent way to smuggle sensitive plans inside the most nonsensical of rhymes. This power is distinct from the Toreador trick known as Doubletalk, which hides a whole sentence inside conversational filler rather than splitting a single utterance into two different messages for two different audiences.

System: The power lasts one turn per Willpower Trait spent. The Storyteller determines how well the true message was conveyed to the intended listener based on the acting player's Subterfuge.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book One: Artisans (Toreador)
system.duration: One turn per Willpower Trait spent
